L20@P0: A binary tensor consists of 2n entries arranged into hypercube
L21@P0: format 2 × 2 ×··· × 2. There are n ways to flatten such a
L22@P0: tensor into a matrix of size 2 × 2n−1. For each flattening, M,
L23@P0: we take the determinant of its Gram matrix, det(MMT ). We
L24@P0: consider the map that sends a tensor to its n-tuple of Gram
L25@P0: determinants. We propose a semi-algebraic characterization
L26@P0: of the image of this map. This offers an answer to a question
L27@P0: raised by Hackbusch and Uschmajew concerning the higherorder singular values of tensors.
L28@P0: © 2018 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.
L29@P0: 1. Introduction
L30@P0: The Gram determinants of a real binary tensor of format 2 × 2 ×···× 2(n times)
L31@P0: are an n-tuple of quadratic invariants of the tensor. We introduce the Gram locus, the
L32@P0: locus of tuples that arise as the Gram determinants of a real binary tensor. Here, the
L33@P0: Gram locus is equal to the “set of feasible higher-order singular values”, from [8], under
L34@P0: change of coordinates. The Gram determinants offer a convenient set of coordinates for
L35@P0: studying the higher order singular values of a tensor.

L11: ## Abstract
L12: For a real tensor of format \(2\times\dots\times2\) with \(n\) factors, let \(d_i\) be the determinant of the Gram matrix \(M_iM_i^{T}\) of its \(i\)-th flattening \(M_i\). Seigal called the set of tuples \((d_1,\dots,d_n)\) of tensors in the Frobenius unit ball the Gram locus, described it for \(n=3\), and conjectured that for \(n\ge4\) it is cut out of the cube \([0,1/4]^n\) by a single polynomial inequality \(Q_1\ge Q_2\) (Linear Algebra Appl. 2018, Conjecture 1.5; Oberwolfach Reports 2017).
L13: We point out that this conjecture is false for every \(n\ge4\). For instance, \((9\)\(/100,9\)\(/100,9\)\(/100,6\)\(/25)\) satisfies \(Q_1\gt 500\,Q_2\) but is not the Gram tuple of any real or complex tensor in the unit ball, and the counterexamples form a set with nonempty interior.
L14: This is a short corollary of known results: by theorems of Domanov, Stegeman and De Lathauwer (2017), and of Higuchi, Sudbery and Szulc (2003) for complex tensors, plus an elementary step from the unit sphere to the unit ball, the Gram locus is the set of \(d\in[0,1/4]^n\) with \(\sum_{j\ne i}\sqrt{1-4d_j}\)\({}-\sqrt{1-4d_i}\)\({}\le n\)\({}-2\) for all \(i\).
L15: From this we obtain the correct \(n\)-ary form of Seigal's theorem for \(n=3\), a union of two basic semialgebraic sets given by explicit integer polynomials, and we show that for no \(n\ge3\) is the Gram locus the nonnegativity set of a single polynomial inside the cube (for \(n=2\) it is). We also correct a misprinted inequality in Seigal's theorem for \(n=3\). This is an unrefereed note.
